security_spec.violation_condition: When a Zisb-capable hart executes a conditional branch that guards a dependent load touching security-critical data (e.g., uaccess bounds check indexed memory access, user-register-gated indirect function pointer load, stack-stored function pointer followed by load that may bypass that store via memory disambiguation), and no TEB/MDB/DPB barrier is placed between the guard and the dependent load, speculative execution may transiently bypass the software security boundary and leak the accessed secret through cache timing.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: conditional branch (bgeu|bltu|beq|bne|beqz|bnez) guarding a security boundary, followed within basic-block reach by a load whose address depends on the guarded value, with zero intervening teb/mdb/dpb barrier instructions
security_spec.summary: Zisb introduces TEB (control-flow), MDB (memory-disambiguation), and DPB (data-value) as strict-contract speculation barriers — not optional hints — encoded via Zimop to close in-domain Spectre leaks; the kernel must emit them at bounds-check sites and store-to-load forwarding boundaries or hardware speculation will violate software security invariants observable through cache side channels.
